svg.title: Allocate Launch Cash Before Buying Capacity
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-cash-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Launch Cash Before Buying Capacity; subtitle: Four buckets reconcile lean, reference, and expanded startup budgets.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values encode the $45,000 reference stack only. The value text supplies comparable $15,000 lean and $90,000 expanded stacks in the same bucket order. These are startup cash allocations, not annual expenses or revenue scenarios. Do not stack all three budgets together.; caption: Lean: $4,500 + $2,000 + $1,000 + $7,500 = $15,000. Reference: $12,000 + $5,000 + $3,000 + $25,000 = $45,000. Expanded: $22,000 + $10,000 + $6,000 + $52,000 = $90,000. A lean launch uses existing transport and staged hiring; none of these budgets proves runway for nine simultaneous starts.; stages: label: Equipment and initial supplies; value: Lean $4,500; reference $12,000; expanded $22,000 equipment cash; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Fund commercial vacuums, carts, microfiber systems, PPE, dispensers, and initial chemicals. Rent infrequent specialty machines until contracted utilization supports ownership. Avoid duplicating client-provided equipment in the budget.; label: Setup and coverage deposits; value: Lean $2,000; reference $5,000; expanded $10,000 setup cash; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Reserve cash for registration, required local licensing, insurance deposits, contract preparation, and initial safety training. Replace estimates with jurisdiction-specific fees and written broker quotations before committing funds.; label: Acquisition and operating systems; value: Lean $1,000; reference $3,000; expanded $6,000 acquisition cash; numeric value: 3000.0; detail: Fund a focused website, local prospect research, walkthrough travel, estimating setup, Swept onboarding, and QuickBooks configuration. Limit subscription seats and advertising commitments until the first route converts.; label: Payroll and collection buffer; value: Lean $7,500; reference $25,000; expanded $52,000 liquidity; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Hold unspent cash for wages, payroll charges, subcontract invoices, and collection delays. At Base-Case direct labor of $435,000 yearly, $25,000 covers about three weeks of direct labor alone; stage mobilization and model all other cash outflows separately.

rect.title: label: Equipment and initial supplies; numeric value: 12000.0; value: Lean $4,500; reference $12,000; expanded $22,000 equipment cash; detail: Fund commercial vacuums, carts, microfiber systems, PPE, dispensers, and initial chemicals. Rent infrequent specialty machines until contracted utilization supports ownership. Avoid duplicating client-provided equipment in the budget.

Replace estimates with jurisdiction-specific fees and written broker quotations before committing funds.

Limit subscription seats and advertising commitments until the first route converts.

At Base-Case direct labor of $435,000 yearly, $25,000 covers about three weeks of direct labor alone; stage mobilization and model all other cash outflows separately.
